text:
The instructor, a serene woman named Serenity who looked like she hadn’t blinked in three years, glided into the room. "Welcome," she whispered, her voice barely disturbing the dust motes. "Today, we seek the stillness of the crane. We seek the grace of the... giraffe."

Jim, a man whose idea of stretching was reaching for the remote without standing up, froze. He had signed up for "Yoga for Beginners: How to Touch Your Toes Without Crying." He had not read the fine print. The class was "Advanced: Contortionism and Zen."

He looked at the woman next to him, who was currently folding herself into a pretzel that defied Euclidean geometry. He looked at the man across from him, who was levitating. Jim looked at his own knees, which were currently making a sound like a bag of chips being crushed.

"Find your center," Serenity intoned.

Jim found his center. It was located somewhere between his stomach and his panic attack.

"Begin with the Tree Pose," Serenity said.

Jim lifted one leg. It wobbled. He lifted the other. He looked like a flamingo that had been struck by lightning. To stabilize himself, he gripped the air with intense concentration. This intense concentration required a significant amount of internal pressure.

A low rumble started in Jim’s abdomen. It wasn't a yoga sound. It was the sound of a digestive system that had recently encountered a burrito from a gas station.

Serenity paused. "Do you hear that?"

The class froze. The levitating man dropped to the floor with a thud.

"It is the sound of your ego breaking," Serenity said wisely.

Jim, sweating profusely, tried to ignore the pressure. He shifted his weight. The pressure shifted with him. He attempted a gentle exhale.

*Prrrrt.*

It was a short, sharp note. Like a squeaky toy being stepped on by a giant.

The woman next to him opened one eye. "Is that... part of the pose?"

"No," Jim squeaked. "It's... a release of tension."

"Good," Serenity said. "Release all tension. Even the... auditory kind."

Jim tried to focus on his breath. In through the nose, out through the mouth. But the gas was not interested in his breathing techniques. It was interested in escape.
